text: Some voices carry further than they should. The lantern is lit.
picture: The Storyteller stands in murky mist, his boots planted on dark earth. His head is bowed, his face shadowed by a low-held red lantern. Far behind him, one small, lonely upstairs window glows yellow in a distant house.
motion: the lantern sways faintly in his grip

text: My daughter Lily is four. She sleeps with the baby monitor on.
picture: Lily sleeps soundly in her small bed under a star-patterned duvet. A soft star-shaped night-light glows on a shelf. On the bedside table, the baby monitor sits with its small red light a steady dot in the calm dark.
motion: her chest rises and falls in sleep

text: Last night, at twelve past three, it crackled.
picture: In the deep dark, a tight close-up shows the baby monitor receiver's small red sound lights jumping erratically. Mara's sleeping form is a blurred, dark shape in the bed beyond its harsh illuminated edge.
motion: the red audio lights flicker and pulse

text: Lily was whispering. "I can't. Mummy will hear."
picture: The baby monitor receiver's red sound lights are frozen, with a faint, grainy texture as if from a quiet audio hiss. It dominates the dark frame, a tiny red light glowing. No person is visible.
sound: a faint, childlike whisper on a hiss

text: Then another voice. Low. Patient. "Mummy is asleep."
picture: A tight shot of the baby monitor receiver on the bedside table, its red light glowing. The room is dark. The device's speaker grille is the focus, as if the low voice is emanating directly from it.
motion: her breath catches in her throat

text: I ran. Her door was shut. Her night-light was off. I had left it on.
picture: In a dim, flickering light from a faulty overhead bulb, Mara stands at Lily's closed bedroom door. Her hand rests on the handle. The space under the door is pitch black, no light from within.
motion: her fingertips press white against the door handle

text: Lily was asleep, facing the wall. Nobody else.
picture: Deep, dark room lit only by grey pre-dawn at a window. In bed, Lily in pale star-patterned pajamas sleeps facing a blank wall. A dead night-light socket is visible. The corners of the room are pools of empty blackness.

text: I sat on her floor until dawn, the monitor in my lap.
picture: A weary Mara sits slumped against the wall on Lily's bedroom floor, the baby monitor receiver held in her lap. Its tiny red LED glows in the dim pre-dawn light from the window.

text: At twenty to five, it crackled again.
picture: A tight shot of the baby monitor receiver in Mara's lap. The small red light is the only point of colour in the grey scene. Mara's hands are tense around the device, her knuckles white.
A shot of Lily's sleeping form from the bed's foot. She lies still in her starry pajamas, unchanged, her back turned. The room remains dark except for the faintest grey light from the window.

text: Then the voice came, so close it touched the microphone. "Mummy's awake now."
picture: Mara is frozen on the floor, her wide eyes fixed on nothing, her face a mask of pure terror. Just behind her shoulder, in the deep black corner of the room, a tall, impossibly thin silhouette of unnatural darkness bends down, its featureless head tilted toward her ear.

text: Lily is five now. She still won't sleep without the monitor. She says he likes to listen.
picture: The Host, the Storyteller, stands alone in his dark hollow, a figure of sorrowful knowing. He slowly lowers a red lantern in his hand. Far behind him, at a great distance, a tiny, glowing red monitor light is visible in an upstairs window of the distant house.
